We answer no. Two symmetric periodic orbits already have different physical mean roofs. The bouncing orbit between two disks has mean \(d-2a\); the triangular orbit visiting all three has mean \(d-\sqrt3a\). Since their difference is \((2-\sqrt3)a>0\), the physical roof is not cohomologous to a constant. A scalar substitution assigns length \(cn\) to every period-\(n\) symbolic owner and cannot reproduce both witnesses. The same calculation gives the sharp two-witness minimax lower bound \((2-\sqrt3)a/2\).

The three-disk-specific contribution is bounded accordingly. It is not a new general cohomology criterion, symbolic determinant theorem, or exact scattering construction. It is an owner- and repetition-preserving audit of the proposed scalar bridge: two exact geometric witnesses settle nontransfer, the minimax bound quantifies its unavoidable error, and the object-typing analysis prevents symbolic, semiclassical, and exact-scattering credit from being reassigned to the physical flow.

The finite computation is used only for solver and reproducibility validation. It replays 747 oriented primitive symbolic owners through length twelve at each of three neighboring geometries, for 2,241 physical-orbit rows, verifies the exact witness formulas in the locked implementation, and checks that the period-two calibration disagrees with the other 744 owners at each geometry. These row counts audit the frozen owner convention, solver output, serialization, and deterministic rebuild. They are not additional proof of noncohomology and do not increase the theorem's scope beyond the two exact symmetric owners.

The analysis proceeds in an order intended to prevent credit transfer between unlike objects. Table~\ref{tab:object-map} distinguishes the physical billiard flow, the unit-roof symbolic suspension, a semiclassical cycle construction, and the exact boundary-channel multiple-scattering determinant by state space, owner, clock or weight, determinant status, and permitted relation. The paper first proves statements internal to the first two relevant types: the no-repeat adjacency determinant for a unit roof and the local half-density formula for a symplectic return map. It then tests only the owner- and repetition-preserving scalar bridge to the continuous physical clock; no equality among the four objects is assumed.

The nearest general cohomological framework is the periodic-orbit obstruction for hyperbolic dynamics: if a roof is cohomologous to a constant, every periodic owner has that same mean roof. We use only this necessary telescoping direction, not a new Liv\v{s}ic theorem \citep[main cohomology criteria]{Livsic1972}.%<!--ref:Livsic1972--><!--anchor:section:main-cohomology-criteria-->
The reciprocal determinant for a finite-type shift is likewise classical \citep[pp.~43--49]{BowenLanford1970},%<!--ref:BowenLanford1970--><!--anchor:page:43-49-->
while flow-zeta and transfer-operator formulations retain the roof and dynamical weights \citep[Secs.~1--3]{Ruelle1976}.%<!--ref:Ruelle1976--><!--anchor:section:1-3-->
For open billiards, the established framework distinguishes symbolic itineraries, classical stability, semiclassical cycle expansions, and exact quantum multiple scattering \citep[Secs.~2--6]{Wirzba1999}.%<!--ref:Wirzba1999--><!--anchor:section:2-6-->
Against that background, the manuscript contributes neither the general cohomology obstruction nor the established determinant theories. Its narrower increment is the exact equilateral two-witness test and minimax bound for one owner-preserving scalar-transfer proposal, together with a typed finite replay that validates the implementation without transferring symbolic or semiclassical credit to the physical flow.

Object & State space and owner & Clock or weight & Determinant status and permitted relation \\

Physical billiard flow & Trapped unit-speed billiard; oriented primitive collision orbit & Euclidean flight roof \(T_p\), with repetition \(rT_p\) & No physical determinant is constructed here; the exact two-witness result only rejects a global scalar replacement of this roof. \\
Unit-roof symbolic suspension & No-repeat shift; oriented primitive cyclic word & One unit per collision, so a period-\(n_p\) owner has weight \(z^{n_p}\) & \(\det(I-zA_q)\) is exact for this symbolic object and supplies no physical-flow or quantum determinant credit. \\

The map makes the ownership boundary explicit. A common collision alphabet can organize comparisons, but it cannot identify Euclidean time with symbolic length or turn a semiclassical expansion into the exact boundary-channel determinant.

For each geometry, the replay fixes \(c=d-2a\) from the period-two witness before evaluating other rows. There are three oriented period-two owners, one per unordered disk pair, and all three match. The remaining 744 owners disagree.

These locked counts are solver and reproducibility checks for the declared finite owner population. They are not used as additional proof of roof noncohomology or as evidence for an unbounded owner census.

The repository provides source programs, historical unit tests, frozen owner CSV files, exact witness table, physical replay, JSON summary, receipt, validation note, and a verify-only Round-8 script. Verification checks committed hashes and rebuilds core results without altering evidence. Exact symbolic counts use integer arithmetic; symmetric periods use symbolic radicals; physical coordinates and return maps use high precision with recorded tolerances.

The machine-readable Stage-4 lock at \texttt{experiments/stage4\_reproducibility\_lock.json} pins CPython 3.12.3, NumPy 2.4.4, SciPy 1.16.1, mpmath 1.3.0, the platform assumptions, the current bibliography digest, and a closed 68-file inventory of Round-2--8 sources, tests, inputs, outputs, receipts, and reproduction commands. The matching \texttt{experiments/stage4\_reproducibility\_receipt.json} records the successful validation, and \texttt{bash experiments/reproduce\_stage4.sh} performs a read-only replay with no canonical-refresh path.

In the object map, only the unit-roof symbolic suspension owns the exact adjacency determinant. Its exact primitive ownership and analytic determinant give the typed tuple
\[
 (A0_{\mathrm{fail}},A1_{\mathrm{pass\ analytic}},
 A2_{\mathrm{analytic\ determinant}},A3_{\mathrm{fail}},A4_{\mathrm{fail}}).
\]
The arithmetic route is rejected because no arithmetic source exists by construction, collision parity is merely \(z\mapsto-z\), and no arithmetic Euler factor or spectral target is identified. These A1/A2 credits belong only to the unit-roof object; the semiclassical and exact quantum rows in Table~\ref{tab:object-map} do not transfer them to the physical flow.

The physical flow has a different owner-weight pair: oriented billiard owners carry the nonconstant Euclidean roof \(T_p\). \Cref{thm:nontransfer} refutes only the owner- and repetition-preserving global scalar bridge, so the physical Route-A tuple remains unassigned. It would be wrong to copy symbolic A2, a semiclassical approximation, or the exact boundary-channel determinant into the physical row. A positive physical construction would require a nonconstant-roof operator or flow zeta with a stated function space, domain, and convergence result, followed by a controlled comparison with the separately defined semiclassical and exact quantum objects.

Second, the 2,241-row ledger is finite. It validates frozen words through length twelve, solver behavior, serialization, and deterministic rebuilding, but not asymptotic cycle-expansion convergence, an infinite primitive-owner census, or the full trapped set. The two-orbit proof avoids this finite-cutoff limitation for noncohomology; the replay is reproducibility evidence for the implementation only.

Fifth, the exact multiple-scattering determinant and a classical nonconstant-roof product are distinct even when semiclassical theory relates their expansions. This manuscript does not construct the latter product, establish its functional setting or analytic continuation, or prove a controlled approximation to the former. Thus ``remain open'' in the first limitation means unresolved within this manuscript, not an assertion about the field's global open-problem status. Any future comparison would require explicit limits and estimates; no equality is claimed here.

An exact unit-roof symbolic determinant does not become a physical-flow determinant through one exponential scalar clock. In equilateral three-disk scattering, the period-two and period-three mean flight lengths differ by \((2-\sqrt3)a\). The two exact owners prove that the physical roof is not cohomologous to a constant, exclude every owner- and repetition-preserving substitution \(z=e^{-cs}\), and give the sharp two-witness minimax bound. This is the manuscript's theorem-level three-disk increment within the established cohomology, symbolic-zeta, semiclassical, and multiple-scattering frameworks.

The four-object map keeps the remaining results in their proper types. The \(q\)-symbol determinant and hyperbolic half-density are exact positive statements for the unit-roof symbolic and local stability objects, respectively; neither supplies a physical or quantum determinant. The 2,241-row replay validates the frozen solver, owner convention, serialization, and deterministic rebuild only and is not additional proof of noncohomology. A successor physical construction would need a genuine nonconstant-roof operator with explicit ownership and analytic control before any controlled comparison with semiclassical or exact quantum scattering.
